22507.new_name: Deep-V Embroidered Chemise in Red or Black

22507.desc:
A chemise is the close cousin of the slip — same straight line, slightly more structure at the bust, and a name that sounds like it costs more. This one earns the word: a deep-V front filled with embroidery, a tie detail at the neckline, and a cut that sits between nightdress and lingerie with no obligation to choose.

The embroidery is the craft on display — stitched rather than printed, which is why it survives the wash and the years. It runs along the neckline and follows the deep-V down, placing the detail exactly where the eye goes first. The tie at the neck adjusts the fit of the top by hand, which is the chemise's traditional mechanism.

Red and black are the two offerings, and they split the genre's oldest disagreement: red argues, black implies. Three graded sizes — M, L and XL by weight band — keep the embroidery sitting flat where it was stitched.

The rundown:

  • Fabric: Chiffon with embroidery
  • Style: Deep-V chemise with neck tie
  • Colors: Red, black
  • Sizes: M (40–50 kg / 88–110 lbs), L (50–60 kg / 110–132 lbs), XL (60–70 kg / 132–154 lbs)

Stitched detail, tied fit, two classic colors.

22520.desc:
Butterfly lace on a teddy is the pattern doing the coverage math: where the motif clusters the fabric reads denser, where it thins the piece reads sheerer, and the wearer gets both in one garment without a single design decision visible. This teddy runs the motif across a fitted one-piece body and stops there.

The construction is the genre's simplest — one piece, pull-on, stretch lace doing the fitting — and the butterfly pattern keeps it from reading plain. Black and white versions behave exactly as the colors always do in this category: the black reads as evening, the white as morning, and both as less innocent than they first appear.

One size covers the 40–60 kg band. As a gift it is low-risk and high-hit; as a self-purchase it is the piece that makes the drawer feel complete without adding complexity to it.

Fast facts:

22521.desc:
Cross straps are the quiet workhorse of lingerie design: they add visual interest without adding weight, and they give a plain dress a geometry it would otherwise lack. This nightdress builds its look around them — straps crossing at the front and back of a fitted dress body, with the crossings doing the designing.

The fabric is polyester with real range under the single size: a 70–120 cm bust and 60–90 cm waist, which is a spread that fitted pieces would need three sizes to cover honestly. The straps hold the shape at the crossings, which is where their geometry earns its place — the dress keeps its line because the straps keep theirs.

Black and gray versions split subtle and subtler. Both are nightdress-first pieces that lean lingerie by intent, and both do their crossing in the same places.

22536.desc:
Hollow-out construction and a butterfly motif are natural collaborators: the pattern already implies absence, and the cut-outs simply formalize the arrangement. This teddy takes the partnership to its logical end — a crotchless base under hollow-out lace with the butterfly design running across what remains.

The listing says its piece plainly, and so does the construction: crotchless below, sheer throughout, structured only where the pattern needs a shoulder or a hip to hang from. The polyester-and-lace body has enough stretch to hold the hollow-out edges flat, which is the single engineering demand of the style and the one that separates the design from a torn stocking.

Black and white versions run the two usual directions, and both place the butterflies where the fabric still exists — which is less of the dress than the pattern implies and more than the sheerness suggests.

The specifics:

  • Style: Crotchless one-piece teddy
  • Key details: Butterfly motif, hollow-out cut

22541.desc:
Chain detail on openwork is hardware doing decoration's job: it adds a line of contrast through fabric that is mostly absence, and it does so at a weight that pulls the sheer panels into place. This three-piece set runs the chains across an openwork base, with a top, a T-back panty and a chest patch sharing the design.

The chest patch is the set's signature piece — the element that decides the look's register, and the one with the most agency about leaving. The openwork fabric is see-through by construction and breathable by consequence, which in this style is a genuine feature rather than a euphemism.

One size covers 40–65 kg, with the chains and the openwork both having give. The three pieces match in finish, which is the difference between a set and a kit.

This teddy runs that logic in leather, with leg loops that pull the design's line all the way down.

The leg loops are the signature: elastic loops at the thighs that keep the teddy's hem anchored, which is a structural detail borrowed from dancewear and repurposed here with no pretense about why. The measurements run specific — neck 64–76 cm, bust 67–105 cm, waist 40–66 cm — which in a non-stretch fabric is the difference between fitted and unwearable.

Four colors cover an unusually wide register: pink, black, red and blue, of which the pink is the most committed to the bit. The set reads costume-adjacent at every color, and it does not pretend otherwise.
